decision_reason: NASA's exact ARC-15936-1 catalog entry identifies EUROPA 2.1 as a reusable NASA open-source AI planning and scheduling framework, and the public repository contains substantive code, examples, user documentation, and installation guidance. However, the repository only says that it is under NASA's Open Source Agreement (NOSA); it does not include or identify the exact NOSA version or an agreement file applicable to this repository. In addition, the available project guidance and code history are old, and a current exact-product distribution or operational-use signal was not established. Hold pending a version-specific grant record and current exact-product support/distribution evidence.

government_provenance.note: NASA Software Catalog record ARC-15936-1 names EUROPA 2.1, describes its reusable planning functionality, and identifies the open-source release; the repository README says it was developed at NASA Ames Research Center.

public_source.note: The public repository exposes the framework source, examples, documentation, installation and quick-start links, and publications without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The README asserts NOSA but the repository does not expose a copy or exact version of the agreement. NASA says NOSA is OSI-approved generally, but that does not establish which exact grant version covers this repo. Clearance requires the applicable NASA NOSA grant/version or official repository-specific confirmation.

primary_evidence.note: NASA's catalog confirms the specific versioned product and the README has real user documentation, but the current catalog record and old repository documentation do not establish current exact-product distribution/use or support for this quiet codebase.

product_identity: EUROPA 2.1, a reusable general-purpose planning, scheduling, and constraint-programming framework intended to be embedded in host applications
geography: United States federal aerospace research; NASA Ames Research Center, California
license: Repository README claims NASA Open Source Agreement (NOSA), but the exact version and applicable grant document are unresolved
status_note: Hold. Do not infer NOSA version 1.3 from NASA's general NOSA page. Needed: exact applicable repo grant and current product-specific support/distribution/use evidence.

decision_reason: This is the independently named, reusable cFS File Manager application, not the full Core Flight System framework. NASA's current GSC-18918-1 catalog page identifies File Manager v2.6.0, and the exact public repository contains its C application source plus application-specific user-guide generation instructions. The repository LICENSE is Apache-2.0. NASA records establish a public open-source FM release in 2015; NASA's current cFS v7.0.0 release includes FM changes, providing current support evidence despite the standalone repository's older last source update. Third-party cFS framework components retain their own license and scope.

government_provenance.note: NASA Goddard's 2015 release announcement explicitly lists File Manager Application v2.0 (GSC-16007-1) among the released cFS applications. The repository README identifies FM as a cFS application developed with the NASA Goddard framework.

public_source.note: The public NASA repository exposes FM source, configuration, tests, build files, and documentation. The README states that the application-specific user's guide is generated with Doxygen and names its cFS runtime dependencies.

eligible_license.note: The exact standalone repository LICENSE is Apache License 2.0, an OSI-approved license. NASA's 2015 announcement and the archived FM v2.4.2 SourceForge source distribution establish the earlier public open-source FM release; do not infer that the present Apache text was necessarily the text on the 2015 archive. cFE/OSAL/PSP and other framework components have separate licenses.

primary_evidence.note: NASA's current catalog specifically distributes FM v2.6.0. Its README gives a user's-guide build path, and the current cFS v7.0.0 release documents FM fixes, showing continued support of this exact application within the cFS distribution.

decision_reason: FPRoCK is an identifiable NASA Langley research solver with public source, a NOSA 1.3 grant, installation and usage examples, and documented scholarly use integrated into PRECiSA. However, the exact repository describes a prototype and its source/license history is from 2019; the 2019 paper and current NASA catalog listing do not establish current exact-product operation or support. Hold for a current project-specific distribution, use, or support signal.

government_provenance.note: NASA's exact catalog record names FPRoCK as an open-source release; the NASA NTRS paper was acquired by Langley Research Center, includes a NASA Langley coauthor, and documents integration into the NASA-associated PRECiSA analyzer.

public_source.note: The public repository includes solver source, a v0.1 prototype README, installation and usage instructions, example invocations, and a Docker workflow.

eligible_license.note: The exact repository contains a NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.3 PDF for FPRoCK, the OSI-approved NASA NOSA grant. Its license-file commit is https://github.com/nasa/FPRoCK/commit/a740caef7c6f0fbb6c041ad13c2b28bd6870f045.

primary_evidence.note: The NASA NTRS conference paper documents real use of FPRoCK inside PRECiSA to detect infeasible computational paths, but that evidence is from 2019 and the paper explicitly calls FPRoCK a prototype. The NASA catalog's listing alone does not establish current source use/support.

decision_reason: The NASA-created Generic Urban Air Mobility (GUAM) simulation is an officially distributed, modular research product for UAM/AAM perception, control, and machine-learning research. Its public v1.1 repository has practical execution instructions and examples, and the initial source commit contains the exact NASA NOSA 1.3 grant for catalog release LAR-20229-1. NASA's current software catalog distributes the simulation, and NASA's 2026 GUAM community-challenge call provides current product-family use/support evidence. The license covers NASA-authored repository source; MATLAB/Simulink and other external/proprietary software are not included.

government_provenance.note: NASA's exact catalog record calls this a NASA-created MATLAB/Simulink simulation for UAM/AAM research; the software designation is LAR-20229-1 and its repo README identifies NASA Langley authorship.

public_source.note: The public GitHub repository exposes MATLAB/Simulink model and controller source, demonstrations, and direct execution guidance. The README notes MATLAB/Simulink are called but not included, and users must supply their own licenses.

eligible_license.note: The exact repo includes a NOSA Version 1.3 agreement tied to NASA designation LAR-20229-1; the grant is OSI-approved. Its initial commit https://github.com/nasa/Generic-Urban-Air-Mobility-GUAM/commit/794facc40155c0343a45e688945745b38691d988 contains v1.1 functional source and the grant. MATLAB/Simulink and external libraries are not included under this grant.

primary_evidence.note: The official 2026 AIAA GNC discipline call includes NASA Generic Urban Air Mobility (GUAM) Autonomous Vehicle Community Challenge Problems and NASA POCs; it links to the GUAM repository and the NASA community challenge. This is a current exact-product-family challenge signal. The NASA catalog page provides current versioned distribution, while the repo README gives execution guidance and v1.1 version context.

decision_reason: NASA's exact ARC-17943-1 catalog record and 2019 NTRS paper identify GeoRef as a NASA Ames web tool used for geolocating astronaut ISS photographs, including NASA image products later provided to USGS for disaster-response support. The source is public, but the repo was owner-archived on 2025-06-19 and current exact-code operation or support was not established. The root NOSA 1.3 document designates the original software as GeoCam, while a second Apache-2.0 file is present without clearly scoped file-level coverage; hold until both current product/code parity and license scope are clarified.

government_provenance.note: NASA's catalog identifies the exact GeoRef v1 tool and describes its use for geolocating ISS astronaut photographs; its ARC designation and repository identify NASA Ames provenance.

public_source.note: The public archived repo exposes the Django web application, management code, scripts, deployment/configuration files, and README installation context without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The root LICENSE is NOSA v1.3 but its agreement identifies the NASA Ames original software as GeoCam; a separate LICENSE-2.0.txt is also at the root. The current README does not establish the exact file/component scope of both grants. Do not claim either grant product-wide until the scope is documented.

primary_evidence.note: The NASA 2019 paper documents historical internal GeoRef operation for Crew Earth Observations and delivery of image products to USGS, but it does not establish current operation/support of this exact archived repository. The current catalog page is an exact record but not a contemporary use or support signal.

product_identity: GeoRef v1, a NASA web application for georeferencing astronaut photographs from the International Space Station; not NASA's separate GeoCam component repositories or USGS disaster-response systems
geography: United States federal Earth-science and disaster-response imagery; NASA Ames Research Center, California
license: Root repository shows NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.3 for an original NASA Ames GeoCam designation and a separate Apache-2.0 text; exact scope relationship to GeoRef source is unresolved
status_note: Hold. Repo owner-archived June 19, 2025; the 2019 paper is historical use, not current exact-source parity. Before re-review, clarify scope of the NASA NOSA and Apache documents and establish a currently operated or supported GeoRef deployment tied to this code.
